chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), he said:
Be concerned with eating meat, for it grows meat (muscles), and whoever leaves meat for forty days, his character/temperament will become bad.

key_terms.اللَّحْمُ: Meat (specifically referring to animal flesh consumed as food)
key_terms.يُنْبِتُ: It grows/nourishes (causing to increase or develop)

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of eating meat and the consequence of avoiding it for forty days according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ali (a.s.) highlights the physiological and spiritual benefits of meat consumption, linking physical nourishment to the stability of one's temperament (khuluq). The specific mention of forty days echoes the Islamic concept of a complete lunar cycle or period of transformation, suggesting that prolonged abstinence can lead to physical weakness manifesting as character flaws, a view supported by Shia scholars who balance this with the principle of moderation rather than excess.
